# After the Hall of Fame: Pokémon Emerald NDS

What there is to do once you have entered the Hall of Fame: the event islands and their tickets, the roaming legendaries, gifts, new places and battles. Levels are the ones you meet in this game.

## Back home in Littleroot

After the credits you wake up in your room.

1. Go downstairs. Dad is home and gives you the **S.S. Ticket**. Then Mom turns on the TV: a news flash about a Pokémon in flight. She asks you what colour the announcer said:
   - **Red**: Latias roams Hoenn, and Latios waits on Southern Island.
   - **Blue**: Latios roams Hoenn, and Latias waits on Southern Island.
2. Talk to Mom: a letter from the Lilycove ferry company, with the **Eon Ticket**.
3. Go outside. Prof. Birch is waiting by your door and takes you to his Lab, where your Pokédex becomes the **National Pokédex**. From then on Raikou, Entei, Suicune, Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres roam Hoenn.

The S.S. Ticket lets you board the S.S. Tidal at Slateport's and Lilycove's harbors, to the Battle Frontier ([battles](#battles-after-the-hall-of-fame)).

## Roaming legendaries

| Pokémon | Level | Starts roaming |
|---|---|---|
| Latias or Latios | 44 | after Mom's question (the colour you answer) |
| Raikou | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Entei | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Suicune | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Articuno | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Zapdos | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |
| Moltres | 55 | when you get the National Pokédex |

- **Where:** Routes 110-111 and 117-134. Never in towns, caves or buildings.
- **Meeting one:** on the route where a roamer is, 1 in 4 wild battles in tall grass or on the water is the roamer (never when fishing). With several on the same route, it is one of them at random. A Repel keeps a roamer away only when your first Pokémon's level is higher than the roamer's.
- **They move:** each time you walk from one route or town into the next, every roamer moves to a route next to its own (now and then further away). When you fly, go through a door or load your game, they all jump to new routes at random.
- **In battle:** a roamer runs away as soon as it can. A move or Ability that traps it (such as Mean Look or Shadow Tag) stops it. The damage and status problems you gave it stay after it gets away.
- **Caught:** it stops roaming. **Knocked out:** it is gone until you next enter the Hall of Fame; then it roams again with full HP.
- **Tracking:** a roamer's AREA page in the Pokédex shows the route it is on right now (no area while it is not roaming).

## Event tickets and islands

| Ticket | Who gives it | Island | Pokémon |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eon Ticket | Mom, at home (after Dad gives you the S.S. Ticket) | Southern Island | Latios or Latias (the one that is not roaming), Lv 55 |
| Old Sea Map | Capt. Stern, Slateport City harbor | Faraway Island | Mew, Lv 32 |
| Aurora Ticket | Prof. Cozmo, in his house in Fallarbor Town | Birth Island | Deoxys, Lv 32 |
| Mystic Ticket | Lanette, in her house on Route 114 | Navel Rock | Lugia and Ho-Oh, Lv 78 |

- Each ticket is given the first time you talk to that person after the Hall of Fame.
- Show the ticket at **Lilycove City's harbor** (the Slateport ferry doesn't sail to the islands). With several tickets you choose the island. Every island has a sailor who takes you back to Lilycove.
- The first time you show the Eon Ticket, the ferry sails you straight to Southern Island. After that Southern Island is on the ferry's list for as long as you hold the ticket.
- The first time you show the Old Sea Map, Mr. Briney sails you to Faraway Island himself.

### Southern Island

Walk to the far end of the island and read the stone. Latios or Latias (the one that is not roaming) flies down and battles you. If you run away, it is there again on your next visit. If you knock it out, it flies away and comes back after your next Hall of Fame. Once caught, it is gone. You lose: you black out, and it waits for your next visit.

### Faraway Island

When you go into the grassy middle of the island, Mew sees you and runs into the tall grass. It wanders there; talk to it to battle it.

### Birth Island

Talk to the triangle: it jumps to another spot. Walk to it and talk to it again, in no more steps than the shortest way (4, 8, 8, 8, 4, 4, 4, 6, 3 and 3 steps for its 10 moves). With too many steps it goes back to where it started. The 10th time you reach it in time, it breaks and Deoxys appears. Leaving the island resets the puzzle.

### Navel Rock

Inside, the way forks: up to the summit, where Ho-Oh comes down when you walk up to it, and the long way down to the bottom, where Lugia waits.

### If you run, lose or knock one out (Mew, Deoxys, Lugia, Ho-Oh)

- **Caught:** it is gone from the island.
- **Ran away:** it is there again on your next visit (Deoxys: solve the triangle again).
- **You lose:** you black out, and it waits for your next visit.
- **Knocked out:** it flies away, and comes back after your next Hall of Fame.

## Gifts

- **Beldum** (Lv 5): the Poké Ball in Steven's house in Mossdeep City, after the Hall of Fame. You need room in your party.
- **Jirachi** (Lv 5): the scientist at the back of the Mossdeep Space Center (1F) gives it after the Hall of Fame. You need room in your party.
- **Celebi** (Lv 10): once you have the National Pokédex, it stands in the clearing in the north-east of Petalburg Woods, behind the girl who gives the Miracle Seed. Talk to it to battle it. If you run, it is back next time; if you knock it out, it comes back after your next Hall of Fame.
- **Enigma Berry**: Dad gives you one in Petalburg City Gym after the Hall of Fame (once; not while you already carry one).
- **Diploma**: catch all 200 Pokémon of the Hoenn Pokédex (Jirachi and Deoxys aren't needed) and talk to the game designer on the 2F of the Cove Lily Motel in Lilycove City. He and the rest of the game's staff are there after the Hall of Fame.
- **Cyndaquil, Totodile and Chikorita** (Lv 5): once you have caught 200 of the 202 Pokémon of the Hoenn Pokédex (after the National Pokédex), go to Prof. Birch's Lab: choose one of the three. You need room in your party.

## New places

### Altering Cave

After the Hall of Fame a cave opens in the cliff on the north side of the water on Route 103 (Surf to it). Its wild Pokémon change by the day: Zubat until your first visit, then the next one in this list each new day you pass through Route 103 (after the last, back to the first).

| | Pokémon | Level |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Zubat | 6-16 |
| 2 | Mareep | 3-13 |
| 3 | Pineco | 19-31 |
| 4 | Houndour | 12-22 |
| 5 | Teddiursa | 6-16 |
| 6 | Aipom | 18-29 |
| 7 | Shuckle | 18-29 |
| 8 | Stantler | 18-29 |
| 9 | Smeargle | 18-29 |

### Mirage Island

Not tied to the Hall of Fame: the island shows on Route 130 (between Route 129 and Route 131) on days when the day's number matches a Pokémon in your party (Eggs too). That is 1 in 128 for each Pokémon each day, about 1 in 22 days with six. The number changes once a day. On the island: Wynaut (Lv 5-55) in the tall grass, and a Liechi Berry tree.

### Steven's Cave

After the Hall of Fame the rock in the first room of Meteor Falls is gone, and behind it is Steven's cave. Steven battles you (Lv 84-87; his team is on the [trainers page](trainers-emerald.md#steven)). Beat him once; after that he only talks. If you lose, he battles you again next time.

### Terra Cave and Marine Cave

After the Hall of Fame, talk to the scientist on the Weather Institute's 2F (Route 119). He reports a drought or heavy rain somewhere, a place picked at random each time you come up to his floor:
- **Drought:** a cave entrance opens in a rock wall on Routes 114-116 and 118. It is Terra Cave, with Groudon (Lv 78) at its end.
- **Heavy rain:** rough water on Routes 105, 125, 127 and 129. Dive there to reach Marine Cave, with Kyogre (Lv 78) at its end.
- The weather ends after 1,000 steps; ask the scientist again for a new place.
- Caught or knocked out: it is gone, and its weather ends. Ran away: it is back on your next visit. Once both are caught or knocked out, the scientist has no more reports.

### Desert Underpass

After the Hall of Fame the Fossil Maniac's tunnel on Route 114 opens further. At the far end of the Desert Underpass lies the fossil you didn't take at the Mirage Tower (the Root Fossil or the Claw Fossil). Wild Pokémon there: Ditto, Whismur and Loudred ([wild Pokémon](wild-pokemon-emerald.md#desert-underpass)).

### Safari Zone

After the Hall of Fame the workers leave and two new areas open on the Safari Zone's east side, each with its own wild Pokémon:
- [Safari Zone Northeast](wild-pokemon-emerald.md#safari-zone-northeast): grass Aipom, Teddiursa, Sunkern, Ledyba, Hoothoot, Pineco, Houndour and Miltank; Rock Smash Shuckle.
- [Safari Zone Southeast](wild-pokemon-emerald.md#safari-zone-southeast): grass Sunkern, Mareep, Aipom, Spinarak, Hoothoot, Snubbull, Stantler and Gligar; surfing Wooper, Marill and Quagsire; fishing Magikarp, Goldeen, Remoraid and Octillery.

### Artisan Cave

On the Battle Frontier island: a cave between its east and west halves, with wild Smeargle (Lv 44-55) ([wild Pokémon](wild-pokemon-emerald.md#artisan-cave-1f--artisan-cave-b1f)).

The three chambers open together: in the Sealed Chamber under the sea of Route 134 (Dive), read the braille on the back wall with Relicanth first and Wailord last in your party. Each chamber then has its own braille puzzle.

## Battles after the Hall of Fame

- **The Pokémon League** can be challenged again. The Elite Four and the Champion keep their teams.
- **Wally** waits in Victory Road 1F for a battle (Lv 48-53; his team is on the [trainers page](trainers-emerald.md#wally)). Afterwards he rematches you once a day ([rematches](#rematches)).
- **The Battle Frontier**: take the S.S. Tidal from Slateport or Lilycove with the S.S. Ticket. Rules, Battle Points and prizes: [Battle Frontier page](battle-frontier.md). Black 2's Pokémon World Tournament (PWT) is in the Frontier's Ranking Hall.
- **Trainer Hill** (Route 111) opens after the Hall of Fame; the **Battle Tents** in Verdanturf, Fallarbor and Slateport are open during the story too. Both are on the [Battle Frontier page](battle-frontier.md).
- **Steven** in [Steven's Cave](#stevens-cave).

## Rematches

- **Trainers on the routes:** once you have 5 badges, talk to a trainer from the list below whom you have beaten. Answer YES for a rematch. Each trainer battles once a day, with a team that depends on your badges. Pairs fight a double battle (you need two Pokémon that can battle).
- **Gym Leaders:** after the Hall of Fame, talk to a Leader in their Gym, once a day. Each rematch is a double battle, with a stronger team each time you win (four teams; the last one repeats). Until you have done Wattson's job in New Mauville (he gives you TM24 Thunderbolt), each Leader offers only the first rematch, and Wattson none.
- **Wally:** after the Hall of Fame he waits at the exit of Victory Road 1F. After your first battle there, he rematches you once a day: 3 stronger teams in turn (the last one repeats).
